newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai Bangchak output back to nameplate capacity.
newsitem.headline: Thai Bangchak output back to nameplate capacity.

text.p: Thai refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc raised on Sunday its operating rate to nameplate 120,000 barrel-per-day (bpd), a company official said on Tuesday.
"We were running the crude unit at reduced rates for afew days but it is now running at maximum capacity," the official said.
The company last Wednesday reduced runs by 20,000 bpd due to poor returns and high product stocks.
The official said future operating rates would depend on the level of product stocks.
"We would reduce our crude runs if stocks are high. Otherwise we may have to close the refinery for a few days if there's a ullage problem," he said.
Bangchak would try to run the crude units at full capacity as the company has already committed its crude purchases.
"But in future we may be more conservative in our planning for crude purchases," he said.
The official was pessimistic over Thai oil product demand due to the current monsoon season.
He said that demand could pick up in November when the rainy season is expected to end.
Thai refiners last week lowered their operating rates by between 5-10 percent due to poor domestic demand and high stocks, industry sources said.
The refiners have resorted to exporting surplus products, especially gasoline, at big discounts to quoted Singapore prices due to the lower domestic demand, the source said.
